questions.corrige_markdown: **Hygiene** is the practice of keeping the body, the clothes, the food and the surroundings clean, so as to keep good health and to prevent the spread of diseases.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the various ways of caring for the following body parts, giving a reason for each:

(i) The head and its hairs (ii) The hands (iii) The female genitals *(4, 5, 5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **The head and its hair** (4 ways, any four):
   1. Wash the hair and scalp regularly with soap or shampoo and water, to remove dirt, sebum, dandruff and lice.
   2. Comb or brush the hair every day, to remove dust and tangles and to stimulate the blood supply to the scalp.
   3. Keep the hair short or tidy (plaited), so that it is easy to keep clean.
   4. Do not share combs, brushes, caps or towels, to avoid the spread of lice and of ringworm.
   5. Protect the head with a hat or cap in strong sun, to avoid sunburn.

(ii) **The hands** (5 ways, any five):
   1. Wash with soap and clean water before eating, before handling food and after using the toilet, to remove germs and eggs of worms and so avoid food-borne diseases such as cholera and typhoid.
   2. Cut the finger nails short and clean under them, because dirt and germs collect under long nails.
   3. Do not bite the nails or suck the fingers, to prevent germs from entering the mouth.
   4. Wear gloves when handling chemicals or doing dirty work, to protect the skin from damage and infection.
   5. Treat cuts with an antiseptic and cover them, to prevent germs from entering the wound.
   6. Dry the hands well and use a moisturiser, to prevent cracking of the skin.

(iii) **The female genitals** (5 ways, any five):
   1. Wash the external parts every day with clean water and a mild soap, to remove secretions and avoid odour and infection.
   2. Wipe from front to back after urinating or passing stool, so that bacteria from the anus do not enter the vagina and the urethra.
   3. Change sanitary pads or tampons regularly during menstruation, to prevent the growth of bacteria and odour.
   4. Wear clean, dry cotton underwear and change it every day, because cotton absorbs moisture and allows air in, which prevents fungal infections.
   5. Avoid tight synthetic clothes, and strong perfumed soaps or douching, because they irritate the skin and kill the useful bacteria that protect the vagina.
   6. Do not share towels and underwear, and use a condom, to avoid infections.
